Subject: Hosted API — min spend & burst behavior questions

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran the numbers with our engineering team and have two quick clarifying questions before we can sign off on internal budget:

1) Minimum monthly commitment — does Redwood require a hard minimum dollar spend or a token-based minimum? We currently forecast a baseline of ~120M tokens/mo for steady-state, but expect product launches that spike to ~350–400M tokens for 48–72 hour windows.

2) Burst / on-demand overage pricing — if we commit to a baseline tier but exceed it for short spikes, how are those spikes billed? Is there a grace window or temporary buffer where on-demand traffic is billed at a lower multiplier vs the standard on-demand rate? Also curious whether you do a quarterly true-up or immediate billing for overages.

I attached a simple traffic estimate sheet so you can see the spike shapes we’re planning to support (acme_traffic_estimate.xlsx). We also have procurement questions about having burst terms captured in the MSA (e.g., single clause that caps short spikes).

Can you loop in pricing / account so we can get a clear written option set?

Thanks,
Samantha Lowe

Hi Samantha — thanks for the sheet. Based on ACME’s profile, here are three practical options we typically offer; I included examples so you can model budget impact. All numbers are per-token for generation traffic unless called out.

Option A — Predictable commit (recommended if you want consistent unit economics)
- Commit: 150M tokens/month (minimum spend enforced)
- Effective commit price: $0.00016 / token
- Burst allowance: 1.5x baseline (i.e., up to 225M tokens) for up to 72 cumulative hours per quarter at a reserved-burst rate of $0.00020/token (20% premium over commit price)
- True-up: Monthly true-up against committed tokens; overage beyond commit+burst buffer billed at on-demand rate (see below)
- Example: if you hit 300M in a month, invoice = (150M * $0.00016) + (150M overage charged per rules below) with up to 75M eligible for the burst buffer at the reserved-burst rate.

Option B — Higher commit + lower overage (good for predictable spikes)
- Commit: 250M tokens/month
- Effective commit price: $0.00014 / token
- Burst allowance: 2x baseline for 48 hours per quarter at $0.00017/token
- On-demand (over commit) rate: 1.4x the committed unit price (so $0.000196/token)
- True-up: Quarterly true-up with invoice smoothing option to amortize over the quarter

Option C — Minimal committed floor + on-demand (flexible, lower upfront)
- Commit: 80M tokens/month minimum spend
- Effective commit price: $0.00019 / token on committed volume
- Burst buffer: none built-in; on-demand rate applies to all traffic above commit (on-demand rate $0.00027/token)
- True-up: Monthly

Additional commercial notes:
- Short bursts (<= 72 hours) can be covered under a "burst buffer" clause in the MSA; we can define it either as a fixed token allowance or as a multiplier over baseline for limited windows.
- We offer a one-time grace credit for first-quarter onboarding spikes if you commit (50% of overage capped at $X) — can include in term sheet if helpful.
- For auditability we provide per-route token reports and a 90-day token-level billing CSV for reconciliation.

Next steps: If one of these options looks like a fit, Lauren can prepare a redline-ready term sheet and attach a stub MSA clause for the burst buffer. Happy to run quick examples with your finance team.

—Ben
